name: Saudi Arabian Mining Company (Maaden)
blurb: Saudi Arabian Mining Company (Maaden) is the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's national mining champion, founded in 1997 and headquartered in Riyadh. It operates across four business units — Phosphate, Aluminium, Base Metals & New Minerals, and other segments — mining gold, phosphate rock, bauxite, kaolin, magnesite, copper, and zinc. With a market capitalization exceeding 250 billion SAR, Maaden is one of the largest mining and metals companies in the Middle East and sells into markets spanning India, Europe, the Americas, Africa, and the broader GCC.
recent: Maaden reported Q1 2026 earnings on May 2, 2026, posting EPS of 0.42 SAR on revenue of 8.79 billion SAR. The stock has gained roughly 26% over the past year but pulled back about 7% over the past month, trading near 64 SAR as of May 14, 2026. Full-year trailing net income of 7.43 billion SAR represents a 116% year-over-year increase, reflecting strong commodity pricing and operational leverage.
